messages.subject: Predict() with categorical survey-level covariate in top models
parts:

>blackbear3<-read.csv("BlackBearDetHist.csv", header=TRUE, check.names=FALSE)

>fm<-occu(~cat+hum+month~1, data=bear3)


>newdata<- data.frame(site$cat, mean(site$hum)) #cat and hum are both continuous and I am interest in the "cat" variable here
>newdata$month<-NA

>pred<-predict(fm, type="det", newdata=newdata, appendData=TRUE)

which gives :
Error in X[i, ] : subscript out of bounds

and if it try:
newdata$month<-as.factor("NA")

it gives:
Error in `contrasts<-`(`*tmp*`, value = contr.funs[1 + isOF[nn]]) :

While on this topic, I would also appreciate advice on how to code site-level categorical covariates to keep them constant when using predict(), as my 'trail' covariate has showed up in top models of some other species as well. It seems that this error "contrasts can be applied only to factors with 2 or more levels" will pop up again when I am trying to do that!


Any help on this would be greatly appreciated, I haven't been able to find a similar issue yet in this google group!

Thanks in advance!

messages.subject: Re: Predict() with categorical survey-level covariate in top models
parts:
Hi Carly,

To predict from the detection model you have to provide valid values for all covariates in that model. You can't supply a missing value. So, when generating a prediction you'll need to pick of one of your possible month values. From your call to str() it seems like "10" is a possible value:

newdata<- data.frame(site$cat, mean(site$hum))
newdata$month <- factor("10", levels=levels(obsCovs(bear3)$month))
pred <- predict(fm, type="det", newdata=newdata, appendData=TRUE)

When adding values of a factor to your newdata you should specify all the possible levels of that factor in the original dataset (as I've done above). Otherwise unmarked might generate an incorrect prediction. See this thread for more: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/unmarked/predict$20factors%7Csort:date/unmarked/7KLFSp9QHGE/AhUz6JIdAQAJ.

I didn't actually run this code since I don't have your dataset, but it should get you started at least.

Ken
